searchText: Larger blocks have their own risks with execution time. And I wouldn't want to be in a world where executing a payload takes 3s when we hit TTD cause that will make for some very stressful moments until finalization listening to the Core Dev understanding most of it; newbie question, what is TTD can't really find it on google..... thanks "Terminal total difficulty", it will be used to determine the last block on the POW network and the switch to POS. Is this the same as the difficult bomb? From: https://tim.mirror.xyz/PWFVaHY3Mrx7srarMmuBWya0J5kioR1l2xaH3p5APDk TTD determines when we switch off PoW (the Merge). Difficulty bomb (ice age) is used to force change. See: https://medium.com/ethereum-cat-herders/ethereum-arrow-glacier-upgrade-e8d20fa4c002 Thanks for this - sorry quick follow up - as I understand it’s ropsten fork June 8, then if successful a couple more testnet forks likely in the weeks after and then it would be the mainnet merge if no issues? Is that basically right? Thanks a lot Question - why Ropsten first? Why not Sepolia? Seems weird to me to start with the largest testnet. <dannyryan> Ropsten is to be deprecated soon after it undergoes the transition so it's lowest stakes Why it is going to be deprecated? I would consider the fact that it is the oldest testnet (and thus with the largest state) as a feature. the phrasing of "is a set of codes" is a little weird here
